newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-SBC revamps weak Swiss business.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-SBC revamps weak Swiss business.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp. (SBC) on Wednesday announced a sweeping restructuring of its domestic operations in an effort to restore health to chronically weak Swiss business.

The measures include shedding some 1,700 jobs -- 10 percent of its Swiss workforce -- and write-offs totalling 3.3 billion Swiss francs ($2.65 billion) will push SBC into an expected 1996 loss of 1.9 billion francs.
SBC's move reflects a trend in overbanked Switzerland where the big three Banks have sought to improve a depressed domestic banking sector, battered by the country's sluggish economy.

Financial group CS Holding has already launched a major restructuring, including the cut of 3,500 jobs in Switzerland, and Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), which has been shutting branches quietly, is also working on a plan to revamp its domestic operations.
In addition to reorganising its domestic operations, SBC will radically change the way it calculates possible losses on customer loans and will revalue its own real estate portfolio.
"Once again SBC has shown that it is out in front," said analyst Christoph Bieri of Zurich Kantonalbank, noting the change in calculating provisions is courageous and innovative.

SBC, Switzerland's third largest banking group, expects the restructuring of its domestic division -- including the closure or integration of 80 of 325 branches -- to lead to a boost in earnings of around 400 million francs in the next three years.
SBC chief executive Marcel Ospel said no further measures were planned for the medium term on the domestic side and today's steps should put the group's domestic business on track.
"We think that is pretty much it for the next three years, that is why we can be so specific," Ospel told reporters following a news conference.
The restructuring announced today is the latest chapter in the transformation of SBC from an also-ran into the front-runner of Switzerland's banking big three.
Credit rating agencies gave a nod of approval to SBC's move and analysts and share markets were also positive.
SBC's shares gained 4.25 francs, or 1.8 percent, to 241 francs by mid-session.
Hans Kaufmann, chief analyst and Bank Julius Baer said he would be revising his opinion about SBC in the near future and the 1.7 billion 1997 profit target was a minimum expectation.
"It (the target) is a conservative view," he said.

While SBC's restructuring will push it into the red this year -- compared with 1995's 1.05 billion franc profit -- it is targetting a net profit of 1.7 billion in 1997 and 2.5 billion by 1999 or 2000.

One of the most important goals of the new domestic division is to make the business with corporate clients profitable and central to the new strategy is to have a sharper focus on those customer relationships where there is an opportunity for building a broad-based, long-term partnership.
"In future, a corporate client with a high risk profile will have to pay significantly more than a customer who is deemed to be low risk," SBC said.
Along with the new provision method, credit costs for its corporate customers will reflect the bank's internal rating for them, said Franz Menotti, head of the domestic division.
SBC will also radically change the method of calculating loss provisions to a new system under which default by a loan customer is a predictable risk with a certain probability.

"Losses in the lending business should not be treated as extraordinary, unexpected events but as a cost of doing business which must be anticipated and quantified to the greatest extent possible," SBC said.
As a consequence, SBC will take annual recurring charges of around 600 million francs starting in 1997. This equals the expected annual loss on the existing loan book.

It will also create a one-time general loss reserve -- the ACRA reserve -- of about two billion francs as cushion to enable the bank to absorb unexpectedly high loan losses, for example during times of recession.
($1=1.2450 Swiss Franc)
